welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.body: This app helps you stay well at home after your TMS treatment: short check-ins, small ideas for each day and an easy way to reach your care team.
welcome.disclaimer: This app is not a medical device. It does not diagnose or treat, and it never replaces your care team. In an emergency, call 112.

privacy.title: Privacy center
privacy.intro: In this version, your data stays on this phone. You decide what is collected.

items.checkins: Check-ins: mood, energy, tension, sleep and optional notes — to show your trends.
items.reaction: Tap game: only your average speed and accuracy — tiredness can show up here.
items.movement: Movement: active minutes during exercises — never raw sensor data.
items.location: Location: only whether you're outside during a walk. Coordinates are never saved.
items.where: Where: only on this phone. No account and no cloud yet.
items.sharing: Sharing: your care team only sees a summary when you request a consultation, or if a safety answer needs urgent help.
items.trusted: Trusted person: their name and number stay only on this phone.

privacy.exportBody: Creates a file with everything stored, which you can save or send.
privacy.deleteBody: This removes your check-ins, settings and history from this phone. It can't be undone.
privacy.discreetDesc: Previews only say "A message from Hiillos". They never mention mood or health, because others may see your phone.

ai.title: AI and voice (optional)
ai.llmDesc: Off by default. When on, the messages you type in the chat are sent to our server and to an AI service to write a reply. Check-ins, scores and sensor data are never sent. Crisis words are handled on your phone first and are never sent to the AI.
ai.voiceDesc: Lets you listen to your companion's messages. Only the companion's text is sent to a voice service, never what you write.
ai.unavailable: Not available right now: the app isn't connected to the server, so the built-in companion answers.

shared.title: Learning from others (optional)
shared.label: Start from what helped others
shared.desc: Off by default. When on, Hiillos starts with the small steps that helped other people most, then learns your own. Only one average score per step is used, from several people together. Nothing about you is shared.

embers.bodyReason: On the nights after it, your night-time recovery was higher than your usual.

items.1: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
items.3: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
items.4: Feeling tired or having little energy
items.6: Feeling bad about yourself, or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
items.7: Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
items.8: Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed. Or the opposite: being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
items.9: Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way

reasonsText.moodDrop: Mood decline compared with the previous week
reasonsText.lowMood: Low mood during the recent week
reasonsText.activityDrop: Activity below the personal range (smoothed trend, 3 of the last 5 days)
reasonsText.reactionSlower: Slower reaction times compared with the previous week

wearable.title: Wearable
wearable.menuDesc: Sleep, steps, heart rate and night-time recovery, measured for you
wearable.intro: A watch, ring or band can measure sleep and steps for you, so you have less to log.
wearable.simulated: Simulated for this demo: no real device is paired and all values are synthetic.
wearable.reads: Hiillos reads daily totals only: sleep, steps, resting heart rate and night-time recovery. Never raw signals and never location. Connecting is your consent; you can disconnect at any time.
wearable.use: How Hiillos uses it: measured sleep fills in the nights you did not log. The rules stay the same, and sensors only make Hiillos ask a question.
wearable.recoveryHint: How steady your heart rhythm was while you slept. Compared only with your own usual.

baseline.title: How Hiillos learns your normal
baseline.linkHint: The phases, and where each signal stands today
baseline.intro: Hiillos compares you only with yourself. It takes a few weeks to learn what is usual for you.
baseline.simulated: The data in this demo is simulated.

0.title: During treatment
0.body: With your clinic. Not counted as your normal, because daily visits change your routine. Not in this app yet.

1.title: Averages
1.body: Days 1 to 14. Hiillos learns your usual steps, sleep and time at home, with weekdays and weekends apart.

2.title: Early drift
2.body: Weeks 3 to 8. A smoothed trend is compared with your own range. Regularity is still being learned.

3.title: Full personal picture
3.body: From about week 8. Regularity (how much your days differ) is reliable too.

4.title: Ongoing
4.body: Your usual is updated only from periods a questionnaire confirmed as well.

baseline.share: {{percent}} % is your own data. The rest is a general starting point.
baseline.referenceRule: It never just follows your latest weeks, so a hard stretch cannot become your new normal.
baseline.learning: Still learning. Hiillos needs about three weeks before it compares you with yourself.
baseline.trendsHint: The line is a smoothed trend of the last four weeks. The middle is your usual.
baseline.outside_one: Outside your usual range on {{count}} of the last 5 days
baseline.outside_other: Outside your usual range on {{count}} of the last 5 days
baseline.variabilityOn: Regularity is being used: your reference is long enough.
baseline.variabilityLearning: Regularity needs about eight weeks of your own data. Still learning.
baseline.note: Sensors only make Hiillos ask a question. A questionnaire decides, and a person confirms.
